front: Which bridge, completed in 1937, spans the Golden Gate strait in San Francisco?
back: Golden Gate Bridge — a 2,737m suspension bridge designed by Joseph Strauss, iconic for its International Orange color

front: What is the longest bridge in the world by total length?
back: Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge in China (164.8 km), part of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway, completed in 2010

front: Which medieval bridge in Prague, lined with 30 Baroque statues, crosses the Vltava River?
back: Charles Bridge (Karlův most), built between 1357 and 1402 under King Charles IV

front: What famous bridge in Sydney, Australia is nicknamed 'The Coathanger'?
back: Sydney Harbour Bridge — a steel arch bridge opened in 1932, the world's largest steel arch bridge by deck width

front: Which bridge in London can be raised to allow ships to pass through?
back: Tower Bridge — a combined bascule and suspension bridge opened in 1894, often confused with London Bridge

front: What ancient Roman aqueduct bridge in southern France has three tiers of arches?
back: Pont du Gard — built in the 1st century AD near Nîmes, standing 49m tall, a UNESCO World Heritage Site

front: Which suspension bridge in New York, completed in 1883, was the first steel-wire suspension bridge?
back: Brooklyn Bridge — designed by John Augustus Roebling, connecting Manhattan and Brooklyn over the East River

front: What bridge in Venice, Italy features shops along its entire span?
back: Ponte Vecchio in Florence (not Venice!) — actually, the Rialto Bridge is Venice's most famous. The Rialto Bridge, built 1588–1591, was Venice's first stone bridge across the Grand Canal

front: Which Japanese bridge, rebuilt every 20 years, leads to the Ise Grand Shrine?
back: Uji Bridge (Ujibashi) at Ise Grand Shrine — a 101.8m wooden bridge symbolizing the transition from the everyday to the sacred

front: What is the highest bridge in the world by deck height?
back: Beipanjiang Bridge in China — 565m above the Beipan River in Guizhou province, opened in 2016

front: Which covered bridge design uses a lattice truss pattern and is common in New England?
back: Town lattice truss — patented by Ithiel Town in 1820, using diagonal planks in a crisscross pattern

front: What famous bridge in Istanbul connects Europe and Asia?
back: The Bosphorus Bridge (now 15 July Martyrs Bridge), opened in 1973, was the first bridge across the Bosphorus strait

front: Which bridge in Mostar, Bosnia was destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt in 2004?
back: Stari Most (Old Bridge) — a 16th-century Ottoman bridge over the Neretva River, a UNESCO World Heritage Site

front: What type of bridge uses cables attached directly to towers to support the deck?
back: Cable-stayed bridge — differs from suspension bridges where cables hang from a main cable between towers

front: Which bridge in San Francisco Bay replaced a section that collapsed in the 1989 earthquake?
back: The eastern span of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, replaced with a new self-anchored suspension span opened in 2013

front: What famous natural bridge in Virginia, USA was once owned by Thomas Jefferson?
back: Natural Bridge — a 66m tall limestone arch carved by Cedar Creek, purchased by Jefferson in 1774

front: Which bridge in Portugal is named after a date and crosses the Tagus River in Lisbon?
back: Ponte 25 de Abril — named after the Carnation Revolution of April 25, 1974; opened in 1966, it resembles the Golden Gate Bridge

front: What is a viaduct?
back: A long bridge-like structure carrying a road or railway across a valley, consisting of multiple spans supported by arches or piers

front: Which French viaduct, designed by Norman Foster, is the tallest bridge structure in the world?
back: Millau Viaduct — 343m tall (taller than the Eiffel Tower), crossing the Tarn River valley in southern France, opened in 2004

front: What famous bridge in Florence, Italy has shops built along both sides?
back: Ponte Vecchio — a medieval stone arch bridge over the Arno River, famous for its jewelry shops; rebuilt after a 1345 flood

front: Which bridge connects Denmark and Sweden across the Øresund strait?
back: Øresund Bridge — a combined rail and road bridge-tunnel opened in 2000, 7.8 km long, connecting Copenhagen and Malmö

front: What type of bridge pivots or lifts to allow boat traffic to pass?
back: A movable bridge — types include bascule (drawbridge), swing, vertical-lift, and retractable bridges

front: Which iconic bridge in the Florida Keys was built by Henry Flagler's railroad?
back: Seven Mile Bridge — the original was part of the Overseas Railroad (1912); a modern highway bridge runs parallel (1982)

front: What ancient bridge technique uses a semicircular arch made of wedge-shaped stones?
back: Roman arch bridge construction — using voussoirs (wedge stones) with a keystone at the top, allowing bridges to span wider gaps than beams

front: Which bridge in India, a living root bridge, is grown from tree roots by the Khasi people?
back: The living root bridges of Meghalaya — made from the aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees, some over 500 years old

front: What bridge in China, built during the Sui Dynasty, is the world's oldest open-spandrel arch bridge?
back: Anji Bridge (Zhaozhou Bridge) — built around 605 AD by Li Chun, spanning 50.82m with a remarkably flat arch

front: Which famous bridge crosses the River Kwai in Thailand?
back: The Bridge over the River Kwai in Kanchanaburi — part of the Burma Railway built by POWs during WWII (1943)

front: What engineering innovation allows the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge to withstand earthquakes and typhoons?
back: A pendulum system in each tower and a tuned mass damper system; it's the world's longest suspension bridge at 3,911m main span (opened 1998)

front: Which pedestrian bridge in London wobbles so much on opening day it was temporarily closed?
back: The Millennium Bridge — opened June 2000, closed after 2 days due to lateral sway, reopened in 2002 with dampers installed

front: What bridge in Argentina and Uruguay crosses the Río de la Plata estuary?
back: There is no bridge across the Río de la Plata; a proposed Colonia–Buenos Aires bridge has been discussed but never built. The estuary is crossed by ferry.

front: Which US bridge disaster in 1940 became a famous example of resonance in engineering?
back: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse ('Galloping Gertie') — the bridge oscillated in wind and collapsed on November 7, 1940, in Washington state
